Rashi on Kiddushin 44b:10:1.hebrew: אפי' מיאון אינה צריכה - שאין מעשה קטנה כלום בחיי אביה. ומתמה גמרא: אפילו שידכו, אמר עולא דאף מיאון אינה צריכה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 44b:10:1.english: She does not even require refusal - For the act of a minor is nothing during her father’s lifetime. And the Gemara asks in astonishment: Even if they arranged [a match], did Ulla say that she does not even require refusal?

Rashi on Kiddushin 44b:10:2.hebrew: ומשני דמתני הא לא מתני הא - מאן דמתני פלוגתא דעולא אדשמואל, לא מתני אדשמואל האי פירושא דפריש בה ר"נ — והוא ששידכו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 44b:10:2.english: And [the Gemara] answers: He who teaches this does not teach that - The one who teaches the dispute of Ulla against [the statement of] Shmuel does not teach regarding [the statement of] Shmuel that explanation which Rav Naḥman explained concerning it — "and that is when they arranged [the match]."

Rashi on Kiddushin 44b:10:3.hebrew: איכא דאמרי אמר עולא - מילתא באפיה נפשיה הוא מתני לה, ולא אדרב ושמואל; וסתמא קאמר ליה — ולא שנא שידכו, ולא שנא לא שידכו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 44b:10:3.english: There are those who say [that] Ulla said - He teaches it as an independent matter, and not regarding [the statement of] Rav and Shmuel; and he stated it unconditionally — and it makes no difference whether they arranged [the match] or whether they did not arrange [the match].

Rashi on Kiddushin 44b:12:1.hebrew: אי דקדשה אביה לאחיו במיאון סגי לה - בתמיה — והלא זיכתה תורה לאב בקידושי בתו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 44b:12:1.english: If her father betrothed her to his brother, is refusal enough for her? - [This is said] in astonishment: For did not the Torah grant the father [the right] in the betrothal of his daughter?

Rashi on Kiddushin 44b:12:2.english: Where she betrothed herself - Without her father's consent.

Rashi on Kiddushin 44b:13:1.hebrew: מעשה יתומה בחיי האב - כגון שהשיאה אביה לאחר, ונתארמלה או נתגרשה בקטנותה, שהרי היא בחיי אביה כיתומה, דכיון שהשיאה — אין לאביה רשות בה. ואחרי כן קדשה היא את עצמה לאחי אביה, דהני קידושין בעו מיאון, שלא היה לה להמתין את דעת אביה; ובמיאון סגי להו, דאין מעשה קטנה כלום אלא מדרבנן — דתקון נישואין לקטנה שאין לה אב, שלא ינהגו בה מנהג הפקר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 44b:13:1.english: The status of an orphan in her father's lifetime - For example, where her father married her off to another [man], and she was widowed or divorced while still a minor, for behold, she is like an orphan in her father's lifetime, since once he married her off, her father no longer has authority over her. And afterwards, she betrothed herself to her father's brother, for this betrothal requires refusal, as she had no need to await her father's consent; and refusal suffices for it, because the act of a minor is nothing [by Torah law], except by rabbinic law — for they instituted marriage for a minor who has no father, so that people would not treat her as ownerless property.

Rashi on Kiddushin 44b:14:1.hebrew: אין מוכרה - לבתו, לקרובים שאין להם קידושין בה, דבעינן ראויה לייעוד:
Rashi on Kiddushin 44b:14:1.english: He cannot sell her - [Namely,] his daughter, to relatives with whom betrothal cannot take effect, for we require [that she be] eligible for designation.

Rashi on Kiddushin 44b:14:2.hebrew: מוכרה לקרובים - כדילפינן בפ"ק (לעיל קידושין דף יט:), בתו לאמה — פעמים שאינה נמכרת אלא לאמהות:
Rashi on Kiddushin 44b:14:2.english: He may sell her to relatives - As we derive in the first chapter (above, Kiddushin 19b) [from the verse] “his daughter as a maidservant”: At times she is sold only for servitude.

Rashi on Kiddushin 44b:1:1.hebrew: נערה - לרבנן דאמרי מקבלת את גיטה, מהו שתעשה אחר שליח לקבל את גיטה בחיי אביה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 44b:1:1.english: A young woman - According to the Rabbis, who say [that] she may receive her bill of divorce, what is [the halakha as to] whether she may appoint another [person as an] agent to receive her bill of divorce during her father's lifetime?

Rashi on Kiddushin 44b:1:2.hebrew: כיד אביה כו' - הא דאמרי רבנן דהיא עצמה מקבלת, מאי סבירא להו: ליד אביה מדמו לה, או לחצר אביה מדמו לה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 44b:1:2.english: Like her father’s hand, etc. - As for that which the Rabbis say, that she herself receives [her bill of divorce] — what do they hold: Do they compare her to her father’s hand, or do they compare her to her father’s courtyard?

Rashi on Kiddushin 44b:2:1.english: And is Rava uncertain - That a person of sound mind should have the legal status of a courtyard when he is awake?

Rashi on Kiddushin 44b:2:2.english: [If he is] sleeping and she is guarding him, it is a [valid] bill of divorce - For it is for her a courtyard that is guarded with her knowledge, by her.

Rashi on Kiddushin 44b:2:3.hebrew: ניעור אינו גט - דהויא חצר המשתמרת לדעת העבד עצמו, ואינו דומה לחצר גמורה — דכי אתרבאי חצירה, משום דסתם חצר משתמרת על פי הבעלים, שגדרה סביב ופותח ונועל:
Rashi on Kiddushin 44b:2:3.english: [If he is] awake, it is not a bill of divorce - For [the slave] is a courtyard that is secured with the awareness of the slave himself, and he is not comparable to an actual courtyard — for when [the law of] her courtyard was included, [it was] because an ordinary courtyard is secured by the owner, who fenced it all around and opens and locks [it].

Rashi on Kiddushin 44b:3:1.hebrew: כיד אביה כו' - הא דאמרי רבנן דהיא עצמה מקבלת, מאי סבירא להו — ליד אביה מדמו לה, או לחצר אביה מדמו לה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 44b:3:1.english: Like her father’s hand, etc. - [Regarding] that which the Rabbis say, that she herself receives [her bill of divorce] — what do they hold? Do they compare her to her father’s hand, or do they compare her to her father’s courtyard?

Rashi on Kiddushin 44b:4:1.hebrew: אינו גט עד שיגיע גט לידה - דאין שליחות לקטן. הילכך, המביאו לה יהא שלוחו של בעל להולכה, ויתננו לה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 44b:4:1.english: It is not a bill of divorce until the bill of divorce reaches her hand - For there is no agency for a minor. Therefore, the one who brings it to her is the husband's agent for delivery, and he gives it to her.

Rashi on Kiddushin 44b:5:1.english: If her father said to him - [The father] of a minor girl.

Rashi on Kiddushin 44b:5:2.english: If the husband wishes to retract - [This applies] once [the bill of divorce] was handed over to him.

Rashi on Kiddushin 44b:5:3.hebrew: לא יחזור - דשליח לקבלה הויא הוא, ומשבא גט לידו נתגרשה, ואפילו נשרף הגט מיד:
Rashi on Kiddushin 44b:5:3.english: He cannot retract - For he is an agent for receipt, and once the bill of divorce reaches his hand she is divorced, and even if the bill of divorce was burned immediately.

Rashi on Kiddushin 44b:5:4.hebrew: במה דברים אמורים - דקטנה לא שייך בה שליחות כשאין לה אב, אבל יש לה אב ואמר ליה אביה כו'. כלומר: אבל יש לה אב, שייך בה שליחות ע"פ אביה — אפי' נערה — שאם אמר לו אביה, בין של קטנה בין של נערה: ״התקבל לבתי כו'״. ומהשתא, לא תקשי דיוקא דרישא, דהא בשאין לה אב קאי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 44b:5:4.english: In what case is this said? - That agency does not apply to a minor girl [only] when she has no father; but [if] she has a father, and her father said to him, etc. That is to say: But [if] she has a father, agency applies to her by instruction of her father — even [for] a young woman — for if her father said to him, whether [the father] of a minor or [the father] of a young woman: "Receive [the bill of divorce] for my daughter, etc." And now, the inference from the first clause does not pose a difficulty, for it refers [only to a case] where she has no father.

Rashi on Kiddushin 44b:6:1.hebrew: קטנה שנתקדשה שלא לדעת אביה - לא אמר לה אביה לקבלם, ולא ידע. ובקטנה, הכל מודים שאין קידושיה קידושין שלא לדעתו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 44b:6:1.english: A minor who became betrothed without her father’s consent - Her father did not tell her to accept them [the betrothal tokens], nor did he know [of it]. And in [the case of] a minor, all agree that her betrothal is not a [valid] betrothal without his consent.

Rashi on Kiddushin 44b:6:2.english: She requires a bill of divorce and she requires refusal - As [the Gemara] states the reason below.

Rashi on Kiddushin 44b:6:3.hebrew: אמר קרנא דברים בגו - כך אמר קרנא: יש דברים בתוך דבר זה — כלומר, יש תשובה ותימה בדברי שמואל:
Rashi on Kiddushin 44b:6:3.english: Karna said: [There are] matters within [it] - This is what Karna said: There are matters within this statement — that is to say, there is a refutation and a difficulty in the words of Shmuel.

Rashi on Kiddushin 44b:7:1.english: They said to him - The members of the study hall [said this] to Karna.

Rashi on Kiddushin 44b:7:2.hebrew: הא מר עוקבא ובית דינו בכפרי - שם מקום סמוך לנו. אם נהרדעא ששמואל שם רחוק ממנו, בא ונשאל למר עוקבא. והוא היה אב ב"ד בימי שמואל, כדאמר במו"ק (דף טז:):
Rashi on Kiddushin 44b:7:2.english: Behold, Mar Ukva and his court are in Kafri - [Kafri is] the name of a place close to us. [They said:] If Nehardea, where Shmuel is, is far from us, come and let us ask Mar Ukva. And he was the Av Beit Din [head of the court] in the days of Shmuel, as [the Gemara] says in Moed Katan (16b).

Rashi on Kiddushin 44b:7:3.hebrew: אפכוה ושדרוה לקמיה דרב - בשם קרנא — צריכה גט ומיאון, ובשם שמואל — דברים בגו. ושדרוה לקמיה דרב, לידע אם יודה לדברי שמואל, שהיה חלוק על הדבר. ומשום דרב אוהבו של שמואל היה, אפכוה — אולי יודה לדברי קרנא, שאמרו בשם שמואל:
Rashi on Kiddushin 44b:7:3.english: They reversed it and sent it before Rav - In the name of Karna [they stated]: "She requires a bill of divorce and refusal," and in the name of Shmuel: "There are [questionable] matters within [it]." And they sent it before Rav to know whether he would agree with the words of Shmuel, who differed on the matter. And because Rav was a friend of Shmuel, they reversed it — perhaps he would agree with the words of Karna, which they stated in the name of Shmuel.

Rashi on Kiddushin 44b:7:4.english: Abba bar Abba - He was the father of Shmuel.

Rashi on Kiddushin 44b:8:1.hebrew: וצריכה מיאון שמא לא נתרצה האב בקידושיה ויאמרו כו' - הרואה שהצרכנוה גט סבור שנתרצה האב בקידושיה, והוה ליה גרושתו מעליא, ושוב אין קידושין תופסין לו באחותה — שאחות גרושתו בכרת, דכתיב (ויקרא יח) בחייה, כל שבחייה. ואי קדיש אחותה, אתי לאפוקה בלא גט:
Rashi on Kiddushin 44b:8:1.english: And she requires refusal, lest the father did not consent to her betrothal and they will say, etc. - One who sees that we required her [to receive] a bill of divorce will assume that the father consented to her betrothal, and she is [thus] his full-fledged divorcée, and betrothal with her sister would subsequently not take effect for him — for the sister of one's divorcée is [forbidden under penalty of] excision [karet], as it is written (Leviticus 18:18): “In her lifetime” — as long as she is alive. And if he betroths her sister, he will come to dismiss her without a bill of divorce.

Rashi on Kiddushin 44b:9:1.hebrew: והוא ששידכו - הא דאמר צריכה גט — כששידך בה לאביה קודם קידושין, דאיכא לספוקי שמא נתרצה כששמע, והוו להו קידושין למפרע:
Rashi on Kiddushin 44b:9:1.english: And this [applies only] when they arranged a match - That which [Shmuel] said, [that] she requires a bill of divorce, [applies] when he arranged [a match] for her with her father prior to the betrothal, as there is reason to be in doubt whether perhaps [the father] consented when he heard, and it became a betrothal retroactively.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 44b:10:1.hebrew: מאן דמתני הא - פי' בקונטרס: מאן דמתני פלוגתא דעולא אדשמואל, לא מתני אדשמואל האי פי' דפריש בה ר"נ — ״והוא ששידכו״, אלא סבר דאמר שמואל בלא שידכו, ומש"ה פליג עלייהו. ״איכא דאמרי, אמר עולא: אפי' מיאון אינה צריכה״ — פירש בקונטרס: ״ואפי' שידכו״. וזה דחקו לפרש כן: דאי בלא שידכו דוקא, מאי איכא בין ״איכא דאמרי״ ללישנא קמא? וקשה: דאין זו סברא לומר שתהא חלוקה כל כך, דהא לעיל פריך גמרא: ״אע"ג דשידכו?!״, אלמא סבירא לגמרא שהדבר פשוט הוא דבשידכו צריך מיאון; והכא, ללישנא ד״איכא דאמרי״, אמרי' דלא צריך?! לכך נראה לפרש: דלעולא לא מיירי אלא דוקא בלא שידכו, ויש חילוק בין ״איכא דאמרי״ ללישנא קמא — דלישנא קמא פליג אדרב ושמואל, כדפירש בקונטרס: ״דמאן דמתני פלוגתא דעולא אדרב ושמואל כו'״; ולכך ״איכא דאמרי״ — דכ"ע סבירא דלא פליג אדשמואל, ומילתא באפי נפשיה איתמר בלא שידכו, ומר אמר חדא ומר אמר חדא ולא פליגי:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 44b:10:1.english: "He who teaches this" - The Kuntres Rashi explained: The one who teaches the dispute of Ulla against the statement of Shmuel does not teach regarding Shmuel that explanation which Rav Nachman explained concerning it — "and that is when they arranged the match" — but rather holds that Shmuel spoke where they did not arrange a match, and for that reason Ulla differs with them. "There are those who say, Ulla said: She does not even require refusal" — Rashi explained in the Kuntres: "And even if they arranged a match." And this is what compelled him to explain so: For if it were specifically where they did not arrange a match, what difference is there between "there are those who say" and the first version? And this is difficult: For it is not reasonable to say that the two versions would be so divided, for behold, above the Gemara asked: "Even though they arranged a match?!" From which it is evident that the Gemara held that the matter is obvious that where they arranged a match she requires refusal, yet here, according to the version of "there are those who say", we say that she does not require it?! Therefore, it appears correct to explain: That according to Ulla, his statement deals only specifically where they did not arrange a match. And there is a distinction between "there are those who say" and the first version: For the first version differs with Rav and Shmuel, as Rashi explained in the Kuntres: "The one who teaches the dispute of Ulla against Rav and Shmuel, etc."; and according to this version of "there are those who say", everyone holds that he does not differ with Shmuel, and it was stated as an independent matter where they did not arrange a match, and one Master stated one thing and one Master stated one thing, and they do not disagree.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 44b:12:1.hebrew: אלא דקידשה נפשה וקתני דבעיא מיאון - ותיובתא דעולא, דאמר: "אפילו מיאון אינה צריכה". וא"ת: לשמואל מי ניחא? והא איהו דאמר דבעיא גט בהדי מיאון, והכא קאמר "או מיאנו", דמשמע דלא בעיא גט! וי"ל: בשלמא לשמואל לא ק"ל מידי, דאיכא למימר דלעיל מיירי בשידך והכא מיירי בדלא שידך, ולהכי לא מצריך אלא מיאון. אלא לעולא קשה: דאי מיירי בשידך — גט ומיאון בעי לפי' ר"י ללישנא דאיכא דאמרי, ולפי' הקונטרס אפי' מיאון לא צריך; ואי מיירי בדלא שידך — אפי' מיאון לא צריך, בין לפירוש הקונטרס בין לפי' ר"י:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 44b:12:1.english: "Rather, [is it not] that she betrothed herself, and it teaches that she requires refusal" - And [this is] a refutation of Ulla, who said: "She does not even require refusal." And if you say: Does it work out well according to Shmuel? But wasn't it he who said that she requires a bill of divorce alongside refusal, whereas here [the mishna] says "or they performed refusal," which implies that she does not require a bill of divorce! And one can say: Granted, according to Shmuel it is not difficult for us at all, for one can say that above it is dealing with where they arranged a match, whereas here it is dealing with where they did not arrange a match, and therefore it requires only refusal. However, according to Ulla it is difficult: For if [the mishna] is dealing with where they arranged a match, she requires a bill of divorce and refusal according to the explanation of the Ri for the version of "there are those who say," and according to the explanation of the Kuntres [Rashi], she does not even require refusal; and if it is dealing with where they did not arrange a match, she does not even require refusal, both according to the explanation of the Kuntres and according to the explanation of the Ri.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 44b:6:1.hebrew: קטנה שנתקדשה שלא לדעת אביה - ונראה, דה"ה בנערה איכא חידוש: לר"ל אליבא דר' יהודה, ולר' יוחנן אליבא דכ"ע. והא דנקיט קטנה — משום דבנערה לא שייך למימר "צריכה מיאון", דאין מיאון בנערה; כדאמר (נדה ד' נב.): "עד מתי הבת ממאנת? עד שתביא ב' שערות":
Tosafot on Kiddushin 44b:6:1.english: "A minor who became betrothed without her father’s consent" - And it appears that the same [ruling] applies to a young woman, [and] there is a novelty: according to Reish Lakish in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, and according to Rabbi Yoḥanan in accordance with everyone. And as for that which [the statement] formulated [the case of] a minor, it is because regarding a young woman it is not applicable to say "she requires refusal," for there is no refusal for a young woman, as [the Gemara] says (Niddah 52a): "Until when may a daughter refuse? Until she brings two [pubic] hairs."
